newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish jet crashes into Baltic sea - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Swedish jet crashes into Baltic sea - ministry.

text.p: A Swedish air force jet crashed into the Baltic Sea approximately 120 km (75 miles) southeast of the island of Gotland on Wednesday, a Swedish defence ministry spokeswoman said.

The Viggen surveillance aircraft from an F15 squadron in Soderhamn in central Sweden crashed into the sea at 1145 GMT, the spokeswoman said. Rescue helicopters were at the scene but there was no sign of the pilot, she said.

The spokeswoman declined to confirm reports in Russia's Itar-Tass news agency that the jet had crashed close to a nuclear powered Russian warship, the "Pyotor Veliky". No further details were immediately available.
The accident is the third involving Swedish air force Viggens in the past three months.
On October 10, two air force JA 37 Viggen jets collided in mid air about five kms (three miles) east of the town of Ramesele in central Sweden. Both pilots ejected and were unhurt.
In August, another air force Viggen crashed into the Baltic Sea while on exercises near Ornskoldsvik in northern Sweden. The pilot was killed.

According to the Tass report, quoting Russian naval officials, the Viggen aircraft on Wednesday came down 700 metres (yards) from the "Pyotr Veliky", an atomic cruiser. The Russian ship immediately began searching for the pilot, who was not seen to eject, it said.
Russian navy officials said the Viggen flew over the ship and crashed when the pilot lost control of the plane as he tried to make a sharp right-hand turn at low altitude.
